**On-call handoff — gateway 503s**

**Root cause**
`dep-4471` (gateway, a.novak, 02:12–02:14 UTC): "config: connection-per-request for pool isolation." It flipped `gateway.pool.perRequest` from `false` to `true` and bumped `gateway.timeout.upstreamMs` from 2000 to 2500. Pool size stayed fixed at 20 connections, so once each request started claiming its own connection, the pool maxed out and everything behind it queued.

**Impact window**
Started 2026-03-14 02:14:19 UTC, about 30 seconds after the config took effect. Still ongoing as of the last log entry, 03:59:44 UTC — 548 failed requests (`503`, `ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED`) and climbing, wait queue grew from 13 to 74+. Affected routes: `/v1/cart`, `/v1/session`, `/v1/checkout`, `/v1/orders`, `/v1/catalog/search`, across all four backend services. `/health` kept returning 200 the whole time, so this wouldn't have tripped basic uptime checks.

**Not affected**
Worker fleet (`logs/worker.log`) stayed clean through the same window — no errors, no 503s, jobs finishing normally.

**Rollback**
Roll back `dep-4471` on gateway — revert `gateway.pool.perRequest` to `false` (and `gateway.timeout.upstreamMs` back to 2000 if bundled). No other deploy near the window touches the gateway.
